what: The heuristic identifies customers and the depot from goal fact names, precomputes their location and visited facts, and reconstructs the routing matrix from grounded visit and return-to-depot operator names using metric_operator_cost_from_initial_values. At evaluation it finds the current location and unvisited customers. If exact capacity and all exact demand PNEs survived translation, it computes a capacity-aware greedy route completion using the current load, explicitly adding depot returns when no customer fits, checking aggregate fleet feasibility when max_vehicles is available. Otherwise it computes a pure routing estimate by blending a nearest-neighbor completion from the current location back to the depot with an MST over the remaining routing nodes. Missing folded resource PNEs never prevent construction of the routing heuristic.
why: CVRP states are dominated by the geometry of the current endpoint, the unvisited set, mandatory depot return, and—when exposed by translation—vehicle capacity. Grounded operators provide a reliable, instance-independent source of arc costs, unlike potentially folded travel-cost expressions. A nearest-neighbor completion gives stronger route-order guidance than a simple goal count, while the MST component reduces sensitivity to poor greedy choices. The optional capacity-aware simulation reflects the domain's visit versus visit-via-depot structure and is especially useful on the representative low-capacity, multi-route instances; the routing-only fallback remains effective on instances where capacity, demand, and fleet-limit PNEs have been folded away.
